Tests assert operation categories, permission failures, status and error codes, error messages, response metadata, affected-target summaries, and JSON result shapes.
Dry-run tests prove project data, runtime data, preview state, dirty state, revisions, and history remain unchanged.
Review tests prove queueing, monotonic review IDs, approve/reject behavior, and execution of the originally reviewed command.
Undo/redo tests preserve existing grouping and merge behavior for user and agent edits.
Compatibility tests prove byte-identical .marrow serialization and logically equivalent .mskl/.mbin exports for unchanged fixtures.
Runtime fixture and renderer --skip-render preparation continue to pass for the checked-in player_idle assets without fixture rewrites.

stories.title: Unify editor mutations under session history
stories.description: Introduce the EditorSession transaction and snapshot foundation, route production shell mutations through it, and retire the parallel public ProjectCommand history implementation while preserving current behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: include/marrow/editor/session.hpp introduces a move-only EditorSession and transaction API without UI framework types.
A non-nestable transaction descriptor records edit kind, label, merge key, merge permission, and project/runtime/preview impact flags.
A transaction captures the prior project and preview state and commits one atomic history entry only after validation and any required runtime rebuild succeed.
Cancellation, validation failure, or runtime rebuild failure restores the exact prior project and preview state and creates no history entry.
A no-change transaction creates no history entry and does not change dirty state or revision counters.
History remains capped at 100 entries and preserves the current merge-key and grouped-drag behavior.
Preview skin and attachment composition remains transient and does not mark the project dirty, but remains undoable and redoable.
Production shell edits use the unified session history, and ProjectCommand, ProjectCommandStack, and make_project_command are removed from the public project API and implementation.
Session tests cover rollback, no-change edits, preview-only history, merge behavior, the depth cap, and undo/redo restoration.

stories.title: Move editor playback into a preview controller
stories.description: Move animation selection and preview playback ownership out of shell free functions into a private PreviewController used by EditorSession, without changing frame advancement or visible playback behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: A private PreviewController owns selected animation, playback time, loop, queue, mix, reverse, Skeleton, and AnimationState state.
Seeking, selection changes, preview composition, runtime rebinding, state snapshot, and state restoration are expressed as controller operations rather than shell free functions.
Normal frame advancement remains incremental through AnimationState update/apply and does not rebuild runtime data.
Runtime rebinding after a project edit preserves compatible animation selection, playback time, loop/queue/mix/reverse state, and transient preview composition.
Failed transactions restore the prior preview controller state exactly.
Shell timeline playback and scrubbing use EditorSession preview controls without directly owning Skeleton or AnimationState.
Tests cover animation selection, seeking, incremental advancement, looping, queue/mix/reverse state, preview composition, runtime rebinding, and playback retention across undo/redo.

stories.title: Make EditorSession own authoring state
stories.description: Complete the UI-free EditorSession ownership boundary for project lifecycle, compiled runtime data, preview, dirty state, revisions, history, save, and export, then make ShellState compose it.
acceptanceCriteria: EditorSession exposes open, reload, save, and export_runtime lifecycle operations with actionable errors and no ImGui, GLFW, OpenGL, or shell types in its public header.
Project data, load state, compiled runtime data, PreviewController, dirty baseline, edit transactions, and history are owned by EditorSession.
Callers receive read-only project and runtime access plus preview controls, undo/redo, dirty state, and save/export operations rather than mutable ownership leaks.
Monotonic project, runtime, and preview revision counters advance only for their documented impacts.
Successful save establishes the new dirty baseline, failed save leaves session state unchanged, and export does not silently clear project dirtiness.
Successful and failed open/reload operations have deterministic ownership and rollback semantics.
ShellState composes EditorSession and reacts to revision changes for UI cache, selection, viewport, and file-watcher synchronization.
Session tests cover successful and failed load, dirty baselines, save/export semantics, revision increments, runtime rebuilds, and playback retention.

stories.title: Migrate the C API and agent control to EditorSession
stories.description: Move the opaque C project, socket dispatch, review execution, and agent lifecycle onto EditorSession plus a UI-free AgentControlState while keeping C ABI v1 and the JSON protocol unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentControlState owns pause/terminate state, current operation, activity log, review queue, and monotonic activity/review IDs without shell or UI dependencies.
AgentCommandContext contains EditorSession and AgentControlState references, and the C++ dispatcher signature is dispatch(AgentCommandContext&, Value).
The opaque C MarrowProject owns EditorSession and AgentControlState while every existing C function, status code, ownership rule, and ABI version remains unchanged.
Socket worker threads continue to queue commands only, and all dispatch and mutation remain main-thread single-writer operations.
Review approval executes against the same session/control context and preserves the reviewed command's protocol response.
Project and dispatcher implementation paths no longer include shell_types.hpp or depend on ImGui, GLFW, or OpenGL types.
C ABI and agent characterization smokes pass without changing fixture files, response JSON, or exported data.

stories.title: Drive agent dispatch from one operation registry
stories.description: Replace dispatcher string branching with one registry that binds operation metadata to handlers, generates operations.list, and delegates cohesive handler groups while preserving exact JSON behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: One registry entry owns each operation's name, category, permissions, review requirement, dry-run metadata, and non-null handler.
operations.list is generated solely from the registry and preserves existing operation names, ordering, categories, permission metadata, and response shape.
Dispatcher lookup uses the registry instead of a parallel string if/else chain or independently maintained metadata table.
Handlers are split into inspection, editing/timeline, constraints, and management/validation modules with narrow private interfaces.
Tests reject duplicate operation names and handlerless registry entries.
Every one of the 44 characterized operations resolves to exactly one handler.
Argument validation, dry-run behavior, review routing, status/error messages, response metadata, undo grouping, and exported results remain byte-for-byte or structurally equivalent as appropriate.

stories.title: Extract the timeline shell module
stories.description: Move timeline models, animation editors, scrubbing, and playback controls out of shell_main.cpp into a feature-owned shell_timeline module backed by EditorSession.
acceptanceCriteria: Timeline row/key models, selection state adapters, editors, and timeline window drawing live in shell_timeline source and narrow private headers.
Playback, play/pause, looping, reverse, queue/mix controls, seeking, and scrubbing call EditorSession preview APIs.
Transform, deform, draw-order, event, state-preview, and constraint timeline edits use EditorSession transactions with existing labels and merge behavior.
Timeline selection remains synchronized with hierarchy, inspector, animation selection, and viewport preview.
Immediate edit preview and incremental frame playback preserve current behavior without runtime rebuilds during ordinary advancement.
Editor shell smoke coverage validates playback, scrubbing, keyed edits, grouped undo/redo, and selection synchronization after extraction.

stories.title: Extract the constraint shell module
stories.description: Move constraint selection, default construction, runtime/project conversion, mutation, preview, and panel code into a feature-owned shell_constraints module.
acceptanceCriteria: Constraint type selection, defaults, conversion helpers, mutation helpers, and panel rendering live in shell_constraints source and narrow private headers.
IK, path, transform, and physics constraint authoring continue to use the existing project schema and runtime conversion rules.
All constraint mutations use EditorSession transactions and preserve validation, dirty state, preview rebuild, undo grouping, and redo behavior.
Constraint selection stays synchronized with hierarchy, timeline, inspector, and viewport overlays.
Constraint preview, debug overlay toggles, and runtime export remain externally unchanged.
Editor and project smokes cover the existing create/edit behavior, invalid rollback, immediate preview, undo/redo, and export after extraction.

stories.title: Extract selection and inspector shell modules
stories.description: Separate hierarchy and selection coordination from bone, slot, skin, and attachment inspection/editing so each UI feature owns a narrow module rather than shell_main.cpp globals.
acceptanceCriteria: Hierarchy tree drawing and bone, slot, skin, attachment, animation, and constraint selection synchronization live in a private shell_selection module.
Bone, slot, skin, attachment, and project property inspection/editing live in a private shell_inspector module.
Selection transitions keep hierarchy, inspector, timeline, viewport picking, and agent-driven changes synchronized.
Inspector mutations use EditorSession transactions, preserve immediate preview, and retain current edit labels and merge behavior.
Preview-only skin and attachment composition remains transient, non-dirty, undoable, and visibly synchronized.
Editor shell smokes validate bone picking, hierarchy changes, inspector edits, skin/attachment selection, and grouped undo/redo after extraction.

stories.title: Extract weight-paint and viewport shell modules
stories.description: Move mesh-weight computation and brush gestures into shell_weight_paint, and move viewport window, settings, overlays, camera, picking, and interaction into shell_viewport-owned interfaces.
acceptanceCriteria: Mesh influence lookup, normalization, brush falloff, paint, erase, smooth, heatmap, and stroke gesture state live in a private shell_weight_paint module.
Viewport window composition, framebuffer sizing, camera pan/zoom, picking, settings, debug overlays, onion skins, and interaction routing live behind narrow shell_viewport interfaces.
Paint, erase, and smooth strokes preserve current numeric results, weight normalization, heatmap colors, immediate preview, and one-history-entry gesture grouping.
Viewport selection and gestures remain synchronized with hierarchy, inspector, timeline, and EditorSession revisions.
Viewport renderer, icon, widget, OpenGL, and ImGui code is compiled only for the shell-facing target path.
Editor shell smoke coverage validates paint/erase/smooth, overlays, picking, camera interaction, onion skinning, hot reload, and undo/redo after extraction.

stories.title: Clean up editor shell composition and target boundaries
stories.description: Finish the refactor by extracting project/runtime/agent panels, replacing the God-state compatibility header, removing adapters and duplicate declarations, and enforcing a UI-free marrow_editor library before MAR-127 begins.
acceptanceCriteria: Project lifecycle, runtime/export, and agent activity/review panels live in feature-owned shell modules using EditorSession and AgentControlState interfaces.
shell_types.hpp is removed and replaced by a UI-only shell_state.hpp plus narrow private feature headers without duplicate cross-module declarations.
Transitional project, preview, history, and dispatch adapters are removed after all call sites use EditorSession, PreviewController, AgentCommandContext, and the operation registry.
marrow_editor is UI-free, depends only on marrow_runtime and Zlib, and does not compile shell, icon, widget, viewport, ImGui, GLFW, or OpenGL code.
Shell, icons, widgets, viewport, and platform code compile only into marrow_editor_shell, with icon_registry.cpp compiled exactly once.
shell_main.cpp is responsible only for CLI/platform startup, theme and docking setup, frame composition, and shutdown.
The existing combined C API and renderer targets are not split as part of this story.
C ABI v1, agent JSON, file formats, serialization, fixtures, playback, undo grouping, save/export, hot reload, and visible editor workflows remain unchanged.
The full CTest guardrail and the documented direct C ABI, agent, project, runtime fixture, renderer skip-render, and five-frame editor shell commands pass.

stories.title: Add parameter modeling authoring tools to the editor
stories.description: Build a Parameter Modeling shell mode and shared UI-free authoring primitives after the runtime and editing-P0 gates. Persistent model edits and transient direct-parameter preview use explicit transaction impacts and distinct dirty semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: ShellMode::Parameter preserves the current animation and playhead on entry, stops playback only, and disables Weight Paint plus bone transform gizmos.

PreviewState stores ID-keyed direct parameter values, the active expression, and synthetic amplitude/phoneme input; reload/rebuild preserves surviving IDs, prunes deleted IDs, and initializes new IDs to defaults.
Parameter sliders and numeric inputs are Preview-only, undoable, non-dirty, and never serialized/exported; a continuous slider drag merges into one history entry.

Parameters, Shapes/Deformers, Expressions, and Lip Sync panels provide create/edit/delete and target binding for parameters, groups, blend shapes, warp/rotation deformers, expressions, and lip mappings.
Created stable IDs cannot be renamed; deleting a referenced parameter or a deformer with children is rejected with the dependency list, while deleting a group leaves its parameters intact.

Persistent mutations use one Project|Runtime|Preview transaction that atomically updates dirty state, undo/redo, and runtime preview through common UI-free parameter CRUD, capture_deformer_keyform, create_expression, upsert_lip_sync_mapping, and preview setter primitives.

Lattice-point and rotation-pivot gestures edit one existing keyform in one transaction; if no coordinate keyform exists, a Capture confirmation creates it and applies the gesture in that same transaction.

Capture copies animation-FFD-only offsets for blend shapes, current evaluated lattice for warp, and current angle for rotation; it uses epsilon 1e-9 * max(1, parameter range) and replaces collisions only after explicit GUI confirmation.
ArtPath point authoring, raw mesh vertex sculpting, and keyform copy/mirror are explicitly excluded.
The validated parameter project/shell fixtures cover current-pose entry, transient undo/non-dirty sliders, CRUD/dependency errors, capture confirm/replace, save/reload, and JSON/MBIN runtime export.

stories.title: Expose parameter/deformer authoring through agent commands
stories.description: Expose the exact six-operation parameter authoring surface through the C++ registry and Python MCP facade, sharing MAR-127 UI-free primitives and dry-run candidate validation.
acceptanceCriteria: parameters.list takes no arguments and returns definitions, groups, direct and final values, and counts as read-only inspection.
parameter.set accepts {id,value,dry_run?}, is Preview-only, undoable, and non-dirty, and returns requested, applied, and clamped values.
deformer.create accepts a complete kind-specific typed {deformer,dry_run?}; keyform.capture accepts {deformer,replace?:false,dry_run?} and captures one keyform at the current preview coordinate.
expression.create accepts a complete typed {expression,dry_run?}; lip_sync.map accepts {mapping,dry_run?} and upserts by target parameter.
The five mutation operations are registered with category edit, mutating true, review false, dry_run true, and requires_project true; parameters.list remains read-only.
Dry-run validates project and preview copies plus a candidate runtime build without changing project/preview data, history, dirty state, or revision counters.
parameter.set has Preview impact only; the other four mutations use Project|Runtime|Preview impact and one non-merging undo entry.
keyform capture rejects a coordinate collision unless replace:true is supplied, and bulk capture is not supported.
Mutations preserve the existing via Agent history label and activity log; save and export remain existing explicit reviewed operations.

marrow_agent_dispatch_smoke and tools/mcp/test_client.py compare the exact C++/Python operation-name set, which grows from 49 to 55, and cover dry-run invariants, mutation, undo, candidate rebuild, and export-preview behavior.

stories.title: Add explicit runtime animation clip duration
stories.description: Add optional animations.<name>.duration runtime data while separating authored duration from key-derived duration and preserving existing format and ABI boundaries.
acceptanceCriteria: AnimationData stores optional explicit_duration, exposes inferred_duration(), and keeps duration() as the effective explicit-or-inferred accessor.
The loader accepts a finite non-negative duration no shorter than the last key; absent duration falls back to inference and empty clips are covered.
Loop, queue, complete, reverse, empty-animation, and snapshot behavior consistently uses effective duration.
JSON and MBIN preserve explicit duration without changing .mskl version 1, .mbin version 2, or the C ABI.
Runtime unit tests cover explicit, derived, and empty duration plus playback edge cases.
Fixture smoke and JSON-versus-MBIN inspection prove old-asset fallback and binary equivalence.

stories.title: Author animation clip duration in the editor
stories.description: Persist explicit duration through an ordered set_duration animation edit and one shared UI-free editor and agent mutation.
acceptanceCriteria: Optional .marrow.animation_edits set_duration operations load, save, materialize, and export without affecting old projects or unknown edit families.
The UI edits duration with live preview, dirty tracking, and one undoable EditorSession transaction.
Moving or creating a key past the clip boundary automatically extends duration in the same transaction.
Manual shrink below the last authored key is rejected atomically without changing project, preview, selection, or history.
The C++ operation registry and Python MCP facade expose matching dry-run, validation, affected-animation, mutation, and undo behavior.
Project, shell, agent, and MCP smoke tests cover auto-grow, rejected shrink, undo/redo, save/reload, and JSON/MBIN export.

stories.title: Add a versioned user preference store
stories.description: Introduce an atomically saved user-local JSON store shared by curve defaults and later Recent Projects without coupling preferences to project state.
acceptanceCriteria: A UI-free service loads and saves versioned editor-settings.json with safe defaults for missing or unsupported optional fields.

Production paths are ~/Library/Application Support/Marrow/editor-settings.json on macOS and XDG_CONFIG_HOME/marrow/editor-settings.json, falling back to ~/.config/marrow/editor-settings.json, on Linux.
MARROW_CONFIG_HOME isolates tests from real user preferences.
Saving uses a same-directory temporary file and atomic rename, preserving the last valid file on failure.
Preference activity never dirties a project or enters project history and provides shared typed storage for curve default and recents.
Focused tests cover first run, roundtrip, version handling, malformed input, override isolation, and atomic-save failure.

stories.title: Introduce the typed SelectionSet domain model
stories.description: Replace single optional selection with a UI-free name-based set for imported-rig entities plus one typed active item and legacy compatibility accessors.
acceptanceCriteria: SelectionSet stores Bone, Slot, Attachment, and Constraint selections with at most one active typed member.
Deterministic replace, toggle, range-add, clear, prune, and remap primitives preserve active-member invariants and stable ordering.
Attachment and constraint identities contain sufficient name scope to avoid collisions without introducing stable-ID or topology changes.
Compatibility accessors preserve existing single-selection workflows while migration proceeds.
Selection is transient: it is not serialized and never affects project dirty state or history; unit tests cover mixed sets and invariants.

stories.title: Migrate editor selection consumers to SelectionSet
stories.description: Move shell consumers onto SelectionSet, including source-replacement migration and reusable constraint-identity remap/prune primitives; constraint lifecycle invocation remains owned by MAR-178.
acceptanceCriteria: Hierarchy, inspector, viewport, timeline, constraints, and weight-paint consumers use SelectionSet as their single source of truth.
Reload and atomic runtime-source adoption remap surviving names and prune targets absent from the new imported rig.
SelectionSet exposes tested constraint-identity remap and prune primitives that preserve unrelated selections; MAR-178 invokes them from actual constraint rename/delete transactions.
Compatibility accessors remain only a narrow facade and active-item behavior stays deterministic across preview refreshes.
Project and shell smokes cover reload, missing targets, mixed selection, direct remap/prune primitive behavior, and unchanged dirty/history state without claiming constraint lifecycle integration.

stories.title: Add hierarchy multi-selection gestures
stories.description: Expose platform-correct replace, toggle, visible-range, and additive-range hierarchy gestures over SelectionSet.
acceptanceCriteria: Plain click replaces selection and activates the clicked item; Cmd on macOS or Ctrl elsewhere toggles it with deterministic active fallback.
Shift selects the anchor-to-clicked range in current visible order, excluding filtered and collapsed rows.
Cmd/Ctrl+Shift adds the visible range without clearing existing selections.
Range anchors reset safely when filtering, collapse, or source replacement invalidates them.
Selected and active rendering is distinct, no group transform is added, and shell smokes cover gestures plus dirty/history invariants.

stories.title: Add viewport multi-selection gestures
stories.description: Integrate deterministic viewport hit selection and bone-only box selection while leaving inspectors and gizmos scoped to the active item.
acceptanceCriteria: Point picking uses documented stable precedence across gizmos, bones, slots, attachments, and constraint targets.
Plain and Cmd/Ctrl point gestures replace or toggle the same typed selection shown in the hierarchy.
Dragging empty viewport space performs bone-only replace or additive box selection in stable skeleton order.
Inspector, gizmo, FFD, constraint, and weight tools edit only the active item under multi-selection.
Shell smokes cover overlap precedence, both box directions, additive selection, hierarchy synchronization, and no group or topology editing.

stories.title: Add a parent-space rotation gizmo
stories.description: Rotate the active bone by solving absolute local rotation through the parent transform and auto-keying one transactional gesture.
acceptanceCriteria: The rotation ring uses the inverse parent coordinate system and remains correct with translated, rotated, non-uniformly scaled, and reflected parents.
Continuous angle unwrapping avoids discontinuities at plus or minus 180 degrees and supports deliberate turns beyond 360 degrees.
The gesture auto-keys absolute local rotation through effective-base-track materialization, with live preview and one undo entry.
Singular or non-finite mapping cancels safely and restores the exact pre-gesture state.
Shell and project smokes cover transformed/reflected parents, wrap crossing, active-only editing, cancel, undo/redo, save/reload, and export.

stories.title: Add signed local scale gizmos
stories.description: Scale the active bone with local X, local Y, and uniform handles while preserving signed values, exact zero, and transactional auto-key semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: Local X and Y handles auto-key absolute scale components through the common effective-base-track path.
The uniform handle preserves the gesture-start X-to-Y ratio and signs rather than forcing positive or equal axes.
Negative scale and exactly zero are valid; non-finite values are rejected.
A singular parent or unsolvable pointer mapping cancels the whole gesture without partial project, preview, or history changes.
Shell and project smokes cover reflected/non-uniform parents, sign crossing, zero, ratio preservation, active-only editing, undo/redo, and JSON/MBIN export.

stories.title: Auto-key one FFD vertex in the viewport
stories.description: Edit one existing mesh vertex by materializing the full effective deform and solving attachment-local FFD without changing mesh topology.
acceptanceCriteria: Starting a drag materializes the complete effective deform vector so untouched vertices keep their evaluated offsets.
Unweighted vertices use attachment-local inverse mapping; weighted vertices invert the weighted sum of influencing bone 2-by-2 matrices.
Linked-mesh deform inheritance targets the correct attachment while preserving parent topology and weights.
A singular matrix, invalid identity, or non-finite result cancels before mutation and restores preview exactly.
Shell and project smokes cover weighted, unweighted, linked, and sparse-deform cases plus one-transaction auto-key, undo/redo, and JSON/MBIN export.

stories.title: Edit multiple FFD vertices atomically
stories.description: Add attachment-local vertex selection and move existing selected vertices together with all-or-nothing solving and one gesture transaction.
acceptanceCriteria: Attachment-local click, Cmd/Ctrl toggle, and box gestures select stable vertex identities without creating or editing topology.
Dragging any selected vertex moves the full selected set from one gesture-start snapshot and materializes one complete effective deform key.
If any selected weighted or unweighted vertex has a singular, missing, or non-finite mapping, the entire gesture is rejected.
Vertex selection stays attachment-scoped and clears or remaps safely when skin, source, attachment, or context changes.
Shell smokes cover group movement on weighted/unweighted/linked meshes, mixed-solvability cancellation, one undo entry, save/reload, and export.

stories.title: Share project viewport transform snapping
stories.description: Persist one UI-free project snap model shared by translate, rotate, and scale gestures with opt-in defaults and deterministic modifier behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: An optional additive .marrow snap section defaults off for old projects and stores a 10-unit world grid, 15-degree local-angle snap, and 0.1 absolute-scale snap.
Translate, rotate, and scale use one domain primitive only during active gestures, including signed and exactly zero scale.
Alt always bypasses enabled snapping; Cmd on macOS or Ctrl elsewhere temporarily enables disabled applicable snapping.
Snap settings are transactional project state, while modifier use is transient and does not itself dirty the project.
Project and shell smokes cover all gizmos, default-off compatibility, reflected parents, modifiers, save/reload, and export-neutral settings.

stories.title: Add grid and magnetic FFD vertex snapping
stories.description: Extend shared snapping for FFD gestures with world-grid alignment and 8-pixel screen-space matching against visible mesh vertices.
acceptanceCriteria: FFD movement considers the world grid and all visible mesh vertices within 8 screen pixels after camera and deformation transforms.
Selected vertices are excluded; equal-distance candidates use stable attachment-and-vertex identity ordering.
Magnetic vertex snapping takes precedence over grid snapping whenever an eligible candidate exists.
Alt bypasses both sources and Cmd/Ctrl temporarily enables disabled vertex snapping under the shared rules.
Shell smokes cover threshold boundaries, selected exclusion, tie-breaks, zoom, weighted/linked meshes, vertex-over-grid precedence, group drag, cancel, and undo.

stories.title: Add a synchronized scalar graph view
stories.description: Plot supported continuous timeline components while sharing playhead and key selection with the dopesheet and exposing the runtime's segment-wide easing constraint.
acceptanceCriteria: The graph plots Transform rotation, translation X/Y, scale X/Y, shear X/Y, and Slot R/G/B/A scalar series.
Graph and dopesheet share key identities, selection, active key, and playhead; graph pan and zoom remain transient and duration-independent.
Linear, stepped, and cubic segments are visually distinct.
FFD and discrete lanes are excluded, and the UI states that one outgoing easing is shared across each Transform or RGBA key rather than per component.
Shell smokes cover supported series, exclusions, synchronization, rendering, and the fact that display interactions do not dirty history or add agent operations.

stories.title: Edit graph key time and scalar value
stories.description: Drag graph points through shared authoring primitives so component values, whole-key time, collisions, frame snapping, and duration growth match the dopesheet.
acceptanceCriteria: Vertical drag edits only the active scalar component while horizontal drag changes the entire key's time and all of its components.
Graph editing reuses common frame snap, collision, neighboring-key, stable-identity, and explicit-duration auto-grow rules.
A collision, non-finite value, or invalid context rolls graph and dopesheet preview back atomically.
One drag creates one transaction with live preview, cancel, undo/redo, and stable selection.
Shell and project smokes cover every supported lane family, component preservation, frame snap, auto-grow, collision cancellation, save/reload, and JSON/MBIN export.

stories.title: Edit shared Bezier handles graphically
stories.description: Drag the active key's outgoing shared four-value easing and expose the same UI-free interpolation mutation through agent and MCP surfaces.
acceptanceCriteria: The graph edits the outgoing [cx1, cy1, cx2, cy2] easing with stable normalized-time and scalar-value mapping.
Control-point X values stay in [0, 1], while finite Y overshoot is allowed.
The curve remains segment-wide across Transform or RGBA components; changing the displayed scalar does not create independent curves.
One handle drag is one transaction with preview, cancel, undo/redo, and exact invalid-input rollback.
C++ registry and Python MCP interpolation operations provide matching dry-run, validation, affected-key, mutation, and undo behavior.
Runtime, shell, agent, and MCP tests cover flat and overshoot curves, X limits, linear/stepped conversion, save/reload, and export.

stories.title: Add fixed curve presets and remembered defaults
stories.description: Provide deterministic interpolation presets and store the user's last default curve in the versioned preference service.
acceptanceCriteria: Presets are Linear, Stepped, Ease [0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1], Ease-In [0.42, 0, 1, 1], Ease-Out [0, 0, 0.58, 1], and Ease-In-Out [0.42, 0, 0.58, 1].
Applying a preset to compatible selected keys is deterministic and creates one previewed undoable transaction.
The last chosen default initializes newly authored continuous segments and is atomically stored in editor-settings.json without dirtying the project.
Missing or invalid preference data falls back to Linear and never rewrites existing curves.
GUI, C++ agent, and Python MCP preset application share the interpolation operation and preserve segment-wide easing.
Preference, project, shell, agent, and MCP tests cover constants, MARROW_CONFIG_HOME restoration, undo grouping, save/reload, and export.

stories.title: Add project-local automatic curve handles
stories.description: Store manual or automatic curve intent and a driver component as optional .marrow-only metadata, resolving it to the existing shared runtime easing.
acceptanceCriteria: Optional additive metadata records manual/auto mode and driver scalar, defaulting old projects to manual behavior.
Auto mode applies monotone Fritsch-Carlson tangents to the driver series, including flat and repeated values without non-finite output or unintended overshoot.
Neighbor time/value, driver, retime, and duration changes recompute affected shared curves in the same transaction.
Dragging either handle switches the segment to manual in that gesture; runtime JSON/MBIN export contains only the resolved existing easing and keeps format versions.
Curve-mode mutation has matching C++ agent and Python MCP dry-run, validation, affected-key, mutation, and undo behavior.
Runtime math, project, shell, agent, and MCP tests cover monotone, flat, driver-change, manual conversion, save/reload, and export cases.

stories.title: Synchronize opted-in loop boundary keys
stories.description: Persist lane-level loop synchronization and manage duration-boundary keys only when explicit duration and a time-zero key make the operation unambiguous.
acceptanceCriteria: Optional additive lane metadata defaults off and can enable synchronization only with explicit clip duration and a key exactly at time zero.
Enabling creates or adopts one managed key exactly at duration whose value and shared curve follow the first-key boundary contract.
First-key value or curve, explicit duration, retime, and auto-curve changes update the managed boundary in the same transaction.
Managed identity prevents selection, clipboard, retime, or duration edits from producing duplicate or stale boundary keys.
The UI-free loop-sync operation has matching C++ agent and Python MCP dry-run, validation, affected-lane, mutation, and undo behavior.
Project, shell, agent, and MCP tests cover missing prerequisites, opt-in/out, synchronization changes, save/reload, and JSON/MBIN export.

stories.title: Scale selected key times atomically
stories.description: Scale the current timeline-key selection around the opposite range edge through one shared UI-free retime operation.
acceptanceCriteria: Dragging either selection edge uses the opposite edge as a fixed pivot and accepts finite positive scale ratios only.
Keys with the same event time remain tied, while non-event time collisions and intrusion into unselected neighboring keys reject the entire operation.
Frame snapping and any required explicit-duration growth reuse the common authoring rules and occur in the same transaction.
Preview, cancel, stable selection, undo, redo, and save/reload treat one scaling gesture as one atomic edit.
The C++ operation registry and Python MCP facade expose matching dry-run, affected-key, validation, mutation, undo, and export-preview behavior.
Project, shell, agent, and MCP smokes cover both pivots, event ties, invalid ratios, collisions, neighbor rejection, and JSON/MBIN export.

stories.title: Control transient preview playback speed
stories.description: Add bounded preview speed controls and presets that compose with reverse playback without becoming project authoring state.
acceptanceCriteria: Preview speed accepts finite values from 0.05x through 8x and exposes 0.25x, 0.5x, 1x, and 2x presets.
Speed multiplies preview time progression and composes predictably with the existing reverse toggle, looping, scrubbing, and pause state.
Changing speed is transient and never serializes, dirties the project, enters history, or alters runtime export.
Opening, reloading, or replacing a project resets speed through one documented session default without affecting authored playback data.
Shell smokes cover bounds, presets, forward and reverse progression, loop boundaries, pause/resume, and unchanged dirty/history state; no agent operation is added.

stories.title: Unify manual weight authoring
stories.description: Move brush, numeric, normalization, binding, and agent weight edits onto one UI-free canonical weight primitive.
acceptanceCriteria: Paint, Erase, Smooth, Replace, numeric influence edits, Normalize, Rebind, and agent mutations all use the same domain implementation.
Every result removes non-positive influences, merges duplicate bones, sorts by descending weight then skeleton order, caps at four, and normalizes the sum to one.
The viewport offers a Replace brush, an active-vertex numeric influence table, selected-scope Normalize, and setup-pose Rebind without changing topology.
Invalid bones, non-finite values, empty results, and failed rebinds reject atomically with exact preview rollback and one undo step per accepted gesture or command.
Weight bind and numeric mutations have matching C++ registry and Python MCP validation, dry-run, affected-vertex, mutation, undo, and export-preview behavior.
Unit, project, shell, agent, and MCP tests prove identical canonical output across every manual path, undo/redo, save/reload, and export.

stories.title: Generate deterministic automatic weights
stories.description: Compute repeatable top-four weights for existing mesh vertices from an explicit candidate-bone set in setup pose.
acceptanceCriteria: The operation requires an explicit checked candidate-bone list and never silently expands it to the whole skeleton.
Weights derive from inverse-square distance between each setup-world vertex and each candidate setup-world bone segment.
The closest four candidates are chosen deterministically with skeleton order as the distance tie-break, then pass through the MAR-175 canonicalization rules.
Zero-length segments and isolated or otherwise degenerate vertices fall back to the nearest valid candidate; an empty candidate set rejects without mutation.
GUI and matching C++ registry/Python MCP operations support selected scope, dry-run summaries, one-step undo, and export-preview rebuild.
Unit and smoke tests cover joints, equal distances, zero-length bones, isolated vertices, repeated runs, candidate subsets, save/reload, and JSON/MBIN export.

stories.title: Add constraint lifecycle project operations
stories.description: Represent rename and delete for all four constraint families as ordered optional project-overlay operations without changing runtime format versions.
acceptanceCriteria: Optional .marrow.constraint_edits.operations load and save ordered rename and delete records for IK, path, transform, and physics constraints.
Base-backed constraints use rename operations and delete tombstones, while project-only constraints rename or delete their upsert entries directly.
Materialization applies lifecycle operations deterministically before later upserts and rejects missing sources, duplicate targets, family mismatches, and invalid order atomically.
Old projects and unknown optional project fields retain existing behavior, and runtime .mskl v1, .mbin v2, and C ABI v1 remain unchanged.
Project smoke covers mixed base/project constraints, ordered chains, tombstones, collision rollback, save/reload, merge, and JSON/MBIN export.

stories.title: Expose constraint rename and delete surfaces
stories.description: Connect lifecycle operations for every constraint family to confirmation UI, undoable domain commands, and agent/MCP surfaces.
acceptanceCriteria: IK, path, transform, and physics constraints expose rename and confirmed delete actions with collision and reference previews.
One UI-free lifecycle command atomically cascades runtime root arrays, skins[].constraints, project upserts, ordered operations, and SelectionSet active/selected identities.
Base-backed and project-only constraints produce the MAR-177 representation appropriate to their ownership.
Each accepted GUI action is one EditorSession transaction with preview, dirty state, undo, and redo; cancellation or failure changes nothing.
C++ registry and Python MCP operations provide matching metadata, dry-run, affected-reference summaries, mutation, undo, and export-preview behavior.
Project, shell, agent, and MCP smokes cover all families, skin references, selection remap/prune, collisions, confirmation, rollback, save/reload, and export.

stories.title: Complete constraint parameter widgets
stories.description: Expose the remaining runtime-backed IK and physics fields in the editor and close the IK agent/MCP parity gap.
acceptanceCriteria: IK editing includes softness, compress, and stretch with the same defaults and validation used by runtime parsing.
Physics editing includes step, x, y, rotate, scaleX, shearX, limit, and massInverse.
Every widget uses EditorSession transactions, updates preview immediately, and roundtrips through project materialization and runtime export.
IK C++ operation metadata and Python MCP wrappers expose the previously missing fields with matching validation and dry-run responses.
Project, shell, agent, and MCP smokes cover boundary values, invalid rollback, undo/redo, save/reload, and JSON/MBIN equivalence for all added fields.

stories.title: Make project I/O and source adoption atomic
stories.description: Provide atomic project lifecycle primitives, complete Save As rebasing, and failure-safe runtime-source replacement before adding file dialogs.
acceptanceCriteria: Project save writes a temporary file in the destination directory and atomically renames it so failure preserves the previous file byte-for-byte.
Save As rebases every relative asset, export, atlas-pack, and PSD provenance path against the new project directory while preserving absolute paths.
EditorSession::create and close establish and tear down imported-rig sessions without inventing native rig or topology authoring.
Runtime-source adoption validates and builds the replacement completely before swapping project source, preview, selection, or session ownership.
Project and session tests inject write, rename, validation, and rebuild failures and prove unchanged files and in-memory sessions, plus correct successful rebase/save/reload/export.

stories.title: Add core File path workflows
stories.description: Connect New, Open, Save, and Save As to dependency-free ImGui path modals and the atomic EditorSession lifecycle.
acceptanceCriteria: A native ImGui directory/path modal with no new external dependency drives New, Open, Save, and Save As.
New validates an existing skeleton source, at least one atlas, and a target .marrow path before constructing a session.
A valid New starts a dirty in-memory imported-rig project and does not write the target path until the user explicitly saves.
Open and Save As use MAR-180 atomic adoption and rebasing; invalid input or failure leaves the current session, selection, preview, dirty state, and history untouched.
Shell and project smokes cover path validation, cancel, New without immediate write, Open, Save, Save As, relative references, and failure rollback.

stories.title: Unify dirty-session intent handling
stories.description: Route every session-replacing or terminating intent through one Save, Discard, or Cancel state machine.
acceptanceCriteria: New, Open, Reload, Quit, and native OS close requests enter the same dirty-intent state machine when unsaved changes exist.
Save completes the pending intent only after an atomic save succeeds; Discard performs the intent without persisting current changes.
Cancel keeps the current session and pending intent state available for a deterministic retry or explicit dismissal.
Save failure preserves the current session and pending intent, reports the error, and never falls through to discard, replacement, or shutdown.
Shell smokes cover every intent and response, repeated requests, modal close, save-path cancellation, save failure, OS close, and successful continuation.

stories.title: Persist and manage recent projects
stories.description: Use the versioned preference store to maintain a bounded recent-project list without affecting project state.
acceptanceCriteria: Recent projects are canonical absolute paths, de-duplicated in most-recent-first order, and capped at 10 entries.
Only successful Open, Save As, or the first successful save of a New session records or promotes an entry; failed, cancelled, Reload, and ordinary Save actions do not.
Opening a recent entry uses the MAR-182 dirty-intent flow and promotes the entry only after the project opens successfully.
Missing paths remain visible but disabled, with Remove and Clear Missing actions.
Recent-project preference writes are atomic, never dirty the project or enter undo history, and expose no C++ agent or Python MCP mutation.
Preference and shell tests cover canonicalization, ordering, de-duplication, eviction, missing paths, MARROW_CONFIG_HOME isolation, and failed-action preservation.

stories.title: Add stepped inherit timeline overlays
stories.description: Add an optional project overlay and UI-free merge path for authoring runtime-compatible bone inherit timelines.
acceptanceCriteria: An optional additive .marrow overlay identifies animation, bone, stable key identity, finite non-negative time, and one of normal, onlyTranslation, noRotationOrReflection, noScale, or noScaleOrReflection.
Absent overlay data preserves old-project behavior, and inherit keys are stepped-only with continuous curve data rejected.
Materialization combines imported base timelines and project overlays without mutating shared SkeletonData or losing unrelated animation data.
The UI-free merge primitive produces deterministic effective timelines and reports missing animations, bones, invalid modes, and time collisions before mutation.
Runtime export emits the existing inherit timeline representation in .mskl and .mbin while retaining current format versions and JSON/binary equivalence.
Project and runtime tests cover all five modes, empty/base-backed/project-only timelines, old-project loading, save/reload, merge errors, and export.

stories.title: Complete inherit timeline editing parity
stories.description: Expose inherit keys through the timeline, shared key-editing workflows, and matching agent operations.
acceptanceCriteria: The editor supports Add, Edit, and exact-playhead Remove for stepped inherit keys while preserving stable same-time identities.
Inherit lanes participate in shared key selection, retime, positive time scaling, and typed clipboard workflows with atomic collision and neighbor validation.
Edits use common duration auto-grow and transaction primitives so rejection leaves project, preview, selection, and history unchanged.
Animation rename and delete atomically cascade inherit overlays, key selections, clipboard references, and preview state.
set_inherit_keyframe and remove_inherit_keyframe have matching C++ registry and Python MCP metadata, dry-run, validation, affected-key, mutation, undo, and export-preview behavior.
Project, shell, agent, and MCP tests cover all five modes, add/edit/remove, selection workflows, cascade, undo/redo, save/reload, and JSON/MBIN export.

stories.title: Collect structured project diagnostics
stories.description: Create a shared read-only diagnostic collector with stable identities, typed navigation targets, and allowlisted fix identifiers.
acceptanceCriteria: Each issue has a stable code, severity, message, typed target, and optional safe-fix ID, with deterministic ordering and identity across unchanged revisions.
Collection is UI-free, read-only, and limited to normally opened sessions; partial or degraded first-open diagnostics and automatic correction are excluded.
project.diagnostics preserves error_count, warning_count, project_dirty, and review_queue_count while adding issues and an issue_count.
The collector reports orphan overlays, non-canonical weights, and stale preview references with safe-fix IDs only where applicable.
Typed targets resolve through SelectionSet and panel-focus metadata without mutating selection during collection.
Project, agent, and MCP tests cover deterministic results, severity counts, legacy summary compatibility, typed targets, revision changes, and zero-mutation inspection.

stories.title: Add the Problems view and safe fixes
stories.description: Present structured diagnostics with navigation and a narrowly allowlisted set of undoable repairs.
acceptanceCriteria: The Problems view groups and filters issues by severity and displays collector counts without changing project state.
Activating an issue selects its typed target and focuses the appropriate hierarchy, timeline, inspector, weight, or preview panel when the target still exists.
The view refreshes from project and runtime revisions and handles removed targets without stale selection or crashes.
The only initial fixes are orphan-overlay removal, canonical weight normalization, and stale-preview-reference reset.
Inspection never dirties the project; an explicitly invoked fix uses one validated transaction and one undo entry, with no automatic fix on project open.
Shell and project tests cover grouping, filters, navigation, revision refresh, all three allowlisted fixes, rejection, undo/redo, and inspection invariants.

stories.title: Plan provenance-aware PSD reimports
stories.description: Persist PSD provenance and compute a deterministic staging diff through a UI-free planning API without changing the current project or asset bundle.
acceptanceCriteria: Optional .marrow.editor.import_sources.psd data stores project-relative source provenance and stable mappings from PSD group/name identities to imported layers and runtime targets.
Old projects without provenance still load, while Save As rebases PSD provenance through the MAR-180 relative-path rules.
Planning parses and builds the candidate PSD bundle entirely in staging without modifying project data, runtime sources, history, or target files.
The plan classifies layers as added, updated, or missing using exact group and layer names; it never infers renames.
Missing layers default to preservation, and the deterministic plan exposes stable layer identities and proposed target changes for later review.
Project and PSD tests cover provenance round-trip, relative-path rebasing, nested groups, added/updated/missing classification, duplicate identities, parse failure, and zero-mutation planning.

stories.title: Commit PSD reimports atomically
stories.description: Validate and replace a staged PSD asset bundle through a journaled commit with complete rollback.
acceptanceCriteria: The staged layer directory, textures, atlas, and skeleton are validated together with the current project overlay before any target is changed.
A UI-free commit API replaces all target resources through journaled renames and reports success only after every replacement and runtime-source adoption succeeds.
Parse/build failures and an injected failure after every commit step restore the original target bundle byte-for-byte and leave the active runtime source unchanged.
A successful commit updates PSD provenance and layer mappings while preserving unrelated animation, curve, constraint, inherit, mesh, and editor overlays.

The reviewed import.psd_layers C++ operation and Python MCP tool expose the same dry-run plan, whitelist and approval checks, and execute this commit path after approval instead of merely queueing it.
PSD, agent, and MCP tests cover successful commit, approval boundaries, missing preservation/deletion inputs, overlay preservation, every failpoint, rollback bytes, and journal cleanup.

stories.title: Add the PSD reimport review UI
stories.description: Connect PSD planning and atomic commit to an explicit preview and confirmation workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: The ImGui reimport flow displays source provenance and grouped added, updated, and missing layer changes before enabling confirmation.
Missing-layer deletion checkboxes default off, so missing layers are preserved unless the user explicitly selects them for deletion.
Cancel, modal close, stale-plan detection, planning failure, and commit failure leave the project, runtime source, files, selection, and history unchanged.
Confirmation executes the MAR-189 atomic commit with exactly the reviewed missing-layer choices.
Success adopts the new runtime source while preserving existing unsaved overlays and undo/redo history, then refreshes selection, preview, diagnostics, and provenance safely.
Shell and PSD tests cover preview contents, default preservation, selected deletion, cancellation, stale source changes, successful adoption, overlay/history preservation, and rollback errors.

stories.title: Validate and document Editing P1
stories.description: Run the complete P1 interaction, persistence, export, parity, and rollback suite and synchronize the project documentation.
acceptanceCriteria: End-to-end tests cover duration, selection, gizmos, FFD, snapping, graph editing, loop synchronization, time scaling, playback speed, weights, constraint lifecycle, file workflows, inherit editing, Problems, and PSD reimport.
Old and newly authored projects survive save/reload, and exported .mskl/.mbin assets remain equivalent without changing .mskl v1, .mbin v2, or C ABI v1.

C++ registry and Python MCP parity covers duration, interpolation and curve mode, loop sync, time scaling, weight bind and auto-weight, constraint lifecycle, inherit keys, and reviewed PSD reimport; transient selection, graph display, file dialogs, recents, and playback speed remain unexposed.
Project Save/Save As and every PSD parse/build/commit failpoint prove atomic rollback, including byte-for-byte asset preservation and unchanged active sessions on failure.
The roadmap, editing-gap analysis, architecture description, format specification, and AGENTS.md validation commands reflect the implemented P1 schemas, operations, exclusions, and observed results.
Final validation passes cmake --build build, full CTest plus runtime/editor labels, project/agent/PSD smokes, MCP schema/client checks, renderer --skip-render, and git diff --check.
